title: Cold rebuild: ENTRYPOINT plus CMD
summary: Fix an image's start command on a real Docker Engine, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *CMD and ENTRYPOINT* you fixed an image so that run arguments work, and built it on a
real Docker Engine. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks
are exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The image `greeter2` was built from `CMD ["echo", "hello"]`. What happens with `docker run --rm greeter2 world`?
options: Docker tries to run a program called `world` and fails: `executable file not found`
steps.explain: With only CMD, run arguments replace the whole command, so `world` becomes the program to execute.

steps.title: ENTRYPOINT plus CMD, cold
prompt: A real Docker Engine runs in this terminal. `~/report` has a report tool, `report.sh TEAM`, and a Dockerfile whose
shell-form `CMD sh report.sh everyone` breaks as soon as you pass an argument.
Fix it and build `shop/report:1.0` so that `docker run --rm shop/report:1.0` prints `report for: everyone`,
`docker run --rm shop/report:1.0 ops` prints `report for: ops`, and `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD` are both in exec form.
From memory: no hints this time.
